Description: explicit — validate style JSON with CLI tool after migration
prompt: I'm migrating from Mapbox to MapLibre and want to check whether my exported style JSON is compatible before deploying. Is there a CLI tool I can run on the file?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
### Yes – MapLibre ships a **CLI style-validator** that will tell you whether a Mapbox-exported style JSON conforms to the MapLibre style specification (and therefore can be used with `maplibre-gl`).

| Tool | What it does | How you run it |
|------|--------------|----------------|
| **`@maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec`** (CLI) | Parses a style file, validates every property against the MapLibre style spec, and reports errors/warnings (missing required fields, unknown/unsupported Mapbox-only keys, bad URLs, wrong `source-layer` names, etc.). | `npx gl-style-validate path/to/style.json` |
| **`maputnik`** (optional visual aid) | Loads the same JSON in a GUI so you can see the map while you fix problems that the validator flags. | `npm install -g maputnik` → `maputnik path/to/style.json` |

Below is a step-by-step guide to run the validator and interpret its output.

---

## 1️⃣ Install the validator (one-time)

```bash
# If you already have a project, add it as a dev-dependency:
npm install --save-dev @maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec

# Or just use npx without installing:
# npx gl-style-validate …
```

> **Why a dev-dependency?**  
> The package is only needed at build / CI time, not in the production bundle, so keeping it in `devDependencies` avoids shipping extra code.

---

## 2️⃣ Run the validation

```bash
# From your project root (or any folder that can see the JSON file)
npx gl-style-validate ./styles/my-mapbox-export.json
```

You’ll see output similar to:

```
✔︎ style.json is a valid MapLibre style (0 errors, 2 warnings)

Warnings:
  - source "mapbox-streets" uses a mapbox:// URL (will not load in MapLibre)
  - sprite URL "mapbox://sprites/..." is a Mapbox-only endpoint
```

If there are errors, the CLI exits with a non-zero status code, which is perfect for CI pipelines:

```bash
# Example CI usage
if ! npx gl-style-validate ./styles/style.json; then
  echo "❌ Style validation failed – fix the errors before deploying"
  exit 1
fi
```

---

## 3️⃣ What the validator checks (and what you may need to change)

| Category | Mapbox-only thing that will **error** | What to replace / fix |
|----------|--------------------------------------|-----------------------|
| **Source URLs** | `url: "mapbox://...` | Change to a public or self-hosted vector source, e.g. `url: "https://tiles.openfreemap.org/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf"` or a PMTiles endpoint. |
| **Sprite URL** | `sprite: "mapbox://sprites/..."` | Host the sprite sheet yourself (or use a free public sprite) and point to `https://my.cdn.com/sprite` (no file extension needed). |
| **Glyphs URL** | `glyphs: "mapbox://fonts/..."` | Use a public glyph service (e.g., `https://fonts.openfreemap.org/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf`) or host your own. |
| **Source-layer names** | Names that only exist in Mapbox’s vector tiles (e.g., `road`, `building` from `mapbox://...`) | Verify the new tile source’s layer names (often `road`, `building` are the same, but many providers use `transportation`, `building` etc.). Update the style’s `source-layer` fields accordingly. |
| **Terrain / Fog** | `terrain: {source: "mapbox-dem", ...}` or `fog: {...}` | `terrain` works if you provide a DEM source that you host yourself. `fog` is **not supported** – replace with `sky` (`map.setSky(...)`) and adjust the style’s `sky` object. |
| **Projection** | `projection: "globe"` (Mapbox v2 syntax) | MapLibre uses the same string (`"globe"`), but make sure you are on v5.0+; otherwise remove or set via `map.setProjection({type: "globe"})`. |
| **Free-camera options** | `freeCameraOptions` block | Remove – MapLibre does not have this API. Use `calculateCameraOptionsFromCameraLngLatAltRotation` + `jumpTo/easeTo/flyTo` instead (see the migration guide). |
| **Deprecated properties** | `antialias`, `preserveDrawingBuffer`, `failIfMajorPerformanceCaveat` at top level | Move them under `canvasContextAttributes` in the `Map` constructor. The validator will flag them as errors. |

The validator **does not** automatically rewrite those values; it only tells you where they exist. After fixing the flagged items, run the validator again until you get a clean “0 errors” result.

---

## 4️⃣ Quick “fix-all” checklist after the validator passes

1. **Remove any `mapboxgl.accessToken` line** – MapLibre does not need a token.
2. **Confirm the `style` URL you pass to `new maplibregl.Map({ style: … })` points to the same JSON you just validated.**
3. **Check that all external assets (sprites, glyphs, DEMs) are reachable from the browser** (CORS headers, correct MIME type).  
   - You can test them directly in the browser: `fetch('https://my.cdn.com/sprite.json')` → should return 200.
4. **Run a visual sanity check** with Maputnik (or just load the map in a dev page).  
   - If layers appear missing, double-check the `source-layer` names against the new tile source’s schema (see the *maplibre-source-wiring* skill for a systematic way to discover them).
5. **Add the validation step to CI** so future style edits are caught automatically.

---

## 5️⃣ Example CI snippet (GitHub Actions)

```yaml
name: Validate MapLibre style

on:
  push:
    paths:
      - 'styles/**/*.json'

jobs:
  style-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install validator
        run: npm install --no-save @maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec
      - name: Validate style files
        run: |
          for f in styles/*.json; do
            echo "🔎 Validating $f"
            npx gl-style-validate "$f" || exit 1
          done
```

If any style file fails, the workflow aborts and the PR cannot be merged until the errors are fixed.

---

## 6️⃣ TL;DR – One-liner

```bash
npx gl-style-validate ./my-exported-style.json
```

If the output ends with **“0 errors”**, your JSON is compatible with MapLibre (subject to the manual replacements listed above). If you see errors, edit the JSON (or the source tiles you’ll be using) until the validator reports a clean pass, then you’re ready to deploy.

---

### Need more help?

- **Missing a specific property?** Paste the error line here and I can suggest the exact MapLibre equivalent.  
- **Want to automate sprite/glyph hosting?** I can point you at a simple `express`-based static server or a CDN configuration.  
- **Running into a blank map after the validator passes?** Check the *maplibre-source-wiring* skill – it walks you through CORS, `source-layer` mismatches, and glyph/sprite loading problems.

Happy migrating! 🚀

Description: implicit — tile source with no API key needed during migration
prompt: I'm migrating from Mapbox to MapLibre and removed my access token, but now my mapbox:// style won't load. How can I test my map against a tile service that doesn't require an API key?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
Below is a quick-start checklist you can follow **right now** to get a working MapLibre map without any API key. It uses a public, fully-open vector style that ships its own tiles, sprites and glyphs, so you can verify that the migration (package, namespace, token removal) is correct before you point the map at your own tile source. --- ## 1️⃣ Swap the style URL for a key-free one | What you had (Mapbox) | What to use for testing (MapLibre) | |-----------------------|-------------------------------------| | `style: 'mapbox://styles/mapbox/streets-v12'` | `style: 'https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty'` | | `style: 'mapbox://styles/your-account/your-style'` | Export the style JSON, replace every `mapbox://` source URL with an open source (see the table below) and host it yourself, **or** use the OpenFreeMap URL above as a drop-in replacement. | **Why OpenFreeMap?** * It is a complete vector style (tiles, sprite, glyphs) built on OpenStreetMap data. * No API key, no CORS headaches, and it works out-of-the-box with the default MapLibre CSS. * Perfect for “does the map load at all?” debugging. ### Minimal example ```html MapLibre test – no token
``` Open the file in a browser (or serve it with `npx serve .`). You should see a fully rendered map with streets, labels, and terrain (if the style includes it). If you get a blank map, open the dev-tools console and look for any remaining `mapbox://` references – the style, a source, a sprite, or a glyph URL. --- ## 2️⃣ If you need a different open style, here are a few ready-to-use URLs | Provider | Style URL | What it includes | |----------|-----------|------------------| | **OpenFreeMap** | `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty` | Full-vector OSM style, terrain, sky, glyphs, sprites. | | **MapTiler (free tier)** | `https://api.maptiler.com/maps/streets/style.json?key=YOUR_KEY` | Replace `YOUR_KEY` with a free API key **or** use the public demo style `https://api.maptiler.com/maps/basic/style.json` (no key, limited usage). | | **OpenMapTiles** (hosted demo) | `https://free.tilehosting.com/styles/bright/style.json?key=YOUR_KEY` | Requires a free key; you can also self-host the style & tiles from the OpenMapTiles project. | | **Stamen (raster)** | `https://stamen-tiles.a.ssl.fastly.net/terrain/{z}/{x}/{y}.png` (use as a raster source in a custom style) | Good for quick raster tests; you’ll need to create a tiny style JSON that points to this source. | > **Tip:** If you want to keep the exact same layer names you used in your Mapbox style, export the style JSON from Mapbox Studio, then edit the `sources` section: > ```json > "sources": { > "openstreetmap": { > "type": "vector", > "url": "https://tiles.openfreemap.org/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf" > } > } > ``` > Replace every `mapbox://` source with the `openstreetmap` source (or whichever provider you choose). After that, the rest of the style (layer IDs, paint, layout) can stay unchanged. --- ## 3️⃣ Verify the three “gotchas” that still cause a blank map | Symptom | What to look for | |---------|------------------| | **Console says `mapbox://`** | Search your whole codebase (including the exported style JSON) for the string `mapbox://`. It can appear in `style`, `source.url`, `sprite`, or `glyphs`. | | **CORS or 401 errors** | Those mean a Mapbox token is still being used somewhere (e.g., a custom source you added later). Remove the token and replace the URL with an open endpoint. | | **Missing fonts / icons** | OpenFreeMap already bundles its own glyphs and sprite. If you use a custom style, make sure the `glyphs` property points to a public glyph server (e.g., `https://fonts.openmaptiles.org/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf`) and that the `sprite` URL is reachable. | --- ## 4️⃣ Next steps after the test map works 1. **Pick a production tile source** – see the companion skill **[maplibre-tile-sources](/maplibre-tile-sources/SKILL.md)** for a list of free, paid, and self-hosted options (PMTiles, XYZ, WMTS, etc.). 2. **Export / adapt your own style** – use **Maputnik** (https://maputnik.github.io/) to open the exported JSON, replace the source URLs, and re-publish the style (or host it on a static file server). 3. **Run the style through the validator**: ```bash npm i -D @maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec npx gl-style-validate my-style.json ``` Fix any errors that the validator reports (usually missing `glyphs` or mismatched `source-layer` names). 4. **Swap the test URL for your production URL** in the `style` option of `new maplibregl.Map(...)`. --- ## 5️⃣ Quick “cheat-sheet” of the exact code changes you already made + the one you still need | Before (Mapbox) | After (MapLibre) – what you must still change | |-----------------|-----------------------------------------------| | `import mapboxgl from 'mapbox-gl';` | `import * as maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl';` | | `mapboxgl.accessToken = 'pk.xxx';` | **Delete this line** – MapLibre does not use a token. | | `style: 'mapbox://styles/mapbox/streets-v12'` | `style: 'https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty'` (or your own open style). | | Any `mapbox://` source URLs in a custom style JSON | Replace with the open provider’s URL (see examples above). | | CSS classes like `mapboxgl-ctrl` | Rename to `maplibregl-ctrl` if you wrote custom CSS. | Once those three items are aligned, the map will render exactly as it did with Mapbox (subject to the visual differences of the new style). --- ### TL;DR 1. **Remove the token** – you already did that. 2. **Replace the `mapbox://` style URL** with a public, key-free style, e.g. `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty`. 3. **Run the example** above; if it shows a map, your migration is successful. 4. **When you’re ready**, point the `style` to your own exported style (with all `mapbox://` URLs swapped out) and to the tile source you intend to use in production. If you hit any specific error after swapping the style URL (e.g., `styleimagemissing`, missing glyphs, or 401 responses), drop the exact console message here and I can walk you through the next fix. Happy mapping!

Description: anti-pattern — assuming Mapbox v2 features work in MapLibre
prompt: I was using Mapbox GL JS v2 in my app, including placing the camera at a given longitude, latitude and altitude. After migrating to MapLibre, that code is broken. Did I do something wrong in the migration?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
### What happened? `map.setFreeCameraOptions()` / `map.getFreeCameraOptions()` are **Mapbox-GL-JS v2-only** APIs. MapLibre GL JS never implemented those methods because the fork was made from Mapbox GL JS v1.13 (December 2020). When you migrated the namespace from `mapboxgl` → `maplibregl` the call stayed in the code, but MapLibre simply does not have a `setFreeCameraOptions` function, so you get the runtime error: ``` map.setFreeCameraOptions is not a function ``` That’s not a mistake in your migration – it’s a missing feature that has to be re-implemented with the MapLibre equivalents. --- ## 1️⃣ Replace the free-camera API with the MapLibre workflow MapLibre provides **utility methods** that turn a *camera position* (lng/lat, altitude, bearing, pitch, roll) into a normal `CameraOptions` object that can be passed to `jumpTo`, `easeTo` or `flyTo`. | Mapbox (v2) | MapLibre (v5 + v6) | |------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | `map.setFreeCameraOptions(opts)` | `const cam = map.calculateCameraOptionsFromCameraLngLatAltRotation(lngLat, altitude, bearing, pitch, roll);`
`map.jumpTo(cam);` | | `map.getFreeCameraOptions()` | No direct getter – you can store the last options you passed, or recompute them from the current view if needed. | ### Step-by-step conversion ```js // ---- Mapbox GL JS v2 (broken after migration) ---- map.setFreeCameraOptions({ position: [12.4924, 41.8902, 500], // [lng, lat, altitude] in meters bearing: 45, // degrees clockwise from north pitch: 60, // degrees roll: 0 // degrees (rarely used) }); ``` ```js // ---- MapLibre GL JS (v5/v6) ---- import * as maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl'; // 1. Build the lng/lat array and the extra parameters const lngLat = [12.4924, 41.8902]; // [lng, lat] const altitude = 500; // meters above the ground const bearing = 45; // clockwise from north const pitch = 60; // degrees const roll = 0; // degrees (optional) // 2. Ask MapLibre to translate that into a CameraOptions object const camOpts = map.calculateCameraOptionsFromCameraLngLatAltRotation( lngLat, // [lng, lat] altitude, // altitude in meters bearing, // bearing in degrees pitch, // pitch in degrees roll // roll in degrees (v5.0+) ); // 3. Move the camera – choose the animation you prefer map.jumpTo(camOpts); // instant // or // map.easeTo(camOpts); // smooth, default duration // map.flyTo(camOpts); // “fly” animation ``` **Notes** * `calculateCameraOptionsFromCameraLngLatAltRotation` was added in **MapLibre v5.0**. If you are on an older 1.x compatibility branch you must upgrade to at least v5 (or v6, which is the current stable line). * The method returns a plain `CameraOptions` object (`{center, zoom, bearing, pitch, elevation, roll}`) that works with any of the standard camera-moving methods. * `elevation` is the same as the altitude you passed; MapLibre will compute the appropriate `zoom` level automatically. --- ## 2️⃣ Quick checklist for a successful migration | ✅ Item | What to verify / change | |--------|--------------------------| | **Package** | `npm uninstall mapbox-gl && npm install maplibre-gl` (or `maplibre-gl@1` for a drop-in v1-compatible shim). | | **Import / CSS** | `import * as maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl';` and `import 'maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css';` | | **Namespace** | Replace **all** `mapboxgl` references with `maplibregl`. | | **Access token** | Remove `mapboxgl.accessToken = '…'`. MapLibre does not need a token. | | **Style URL** | Change `style: 'mapbox://styles/…'` to a non-Mapbox style (e.g. `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty` or a self-hosted style JSON). | | **Fog / Sky** | If you used `map.setFog(...)`, replace with `map.setSky(...)` (see the “Fog → Sky” table below). | | **Free-camera** | Use `calculateCameraOptionsFromCameraLngLatAltRotation` + `jumpTo/easeTo/flyTo` (as shown above). | | **Callbacks → Promises** | Methods like `map.loadImage`, `source.getClusterChildren`, etc., now return promises; update `await` or `.then()` usage. | | **Plugins** | Verify each plugin:
• `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-draw` works after CSS class rename (`mapboxgl-` → `maplibregl-`).
• `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-compare` → `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-compare`.
• Geocoder / Directions → use the MapLibre-specific forks (`@maplibre/maplibre-gl-geocoder`, `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-directions`) or other open services. | | **CORS / Glyphs / Sprites** | Ensure the style’s `glyphs`, `sprite`, and any source URLs are not `mapbox://`. Replace with URLs that serve the same assets (e.g., OpenStreetMap-based tiles, your own sprite sheet). | | **Browser support** | MapLibre v6 requires WebGL 2. If you need WebGL 1 fallback, stay on a 1.x compatibility branch (but you’ll miss newer APIs). | --- ## 3️⃣ Fog → Sky (the other common v2-only method) If you also used `map.setFog({color: …, ...})`, the MapLibre equivalent is: ```js map.setSky({ skyType: 'atmosphere', // or 'gradient' / 'solid' skyAtmosphereColor: '#88ccee', // optional, for 'atmosphere' skyAtmosphereHaloColor: '#fff', // optional skyGradient: ['#80a0ff', '#c0d0ff'] // for 'gradient' }); ``` Add a `sky` object to your style JSON if you want the sky to be part of the style (recommended) – see the **Style Specification → sky** section. --- ## 4️⃣ Full minimal example (Mapbox → MapLibre) ```html MapLibre free-camera example
``` Run the page; you should see the map centered on San Francisco, pitched at ~70°, bearing 30°, and elevated 800 m above the terrain. The sky will render instead of the old fog. --- ## 5️⃣ If you still see a blank map or 401 errors | Symptom | Likely cause | Fix | |---------|--------------|-----| | **Blank map** or console shows `mapbox://` | Some part of the style (source URL, sprite, glyphs) still points to Mapbox | Search the whole style JSON for `mapbox://` and replace with a public URL (e.g., `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/...`). | | **401 / 403** from a tile request | A Mapbox token is still being sent (e.g., in a custom source) | Remove `accessToken` and any `?access_token=` query strings. | | **`map.setFog is not a function`** | Still using the Mapbox fog API | Replace with `map.setSky` as shown above. | | **`map.calculateCameraOptionsFromCameraLngLatAltRotation is not a function`** | Using a MapLibre version < 5.0 (or the 1.x compatibility branch) | Upgrade to at least `maplibre-gl@5` (or the current v6). | | **Plugin UI looks unstyled** | CSS class prefixes still `mapboxgl-` | Update your CSS or import the MapLibre-specific plugin CSS (most plugins expose a `maplibregl-` prefix). | --- ## 6️⃣ TL;DR – What you need to do for the camera ```js // Mapbox (v2) – broken after migration map.setFreeCameraOptions({position: [lng, lat, alt], bearing, pitch, roll}); // MapLibre (v5/v6) – correct way const cam = map.calculateCameraOptionsFromCameraLngLatAltRotation( [lng, lat], // lng/lat array alt, // altitude in metres bearing, pitch, roll // optional, default 0 ); map.jumpTo(cam); // or map.easeTo(cam) / map.flyTo(cam) ``` Once you replace the free-camera call with the snippet above (and finish the other migration steps listed in the checklist), the map should work exactly as before—just without a Mapbox access token and using an open tile source. --- ### Need more help? * Which **plugins** does your app use? I can tell you whether they work unchanged, need a CSS rename, or have a MapLibre-specific fork. * Do you have a **custom style** exported from Mapbox Studio? I can walk you through converting the source URLs, sprite, and glyph references. * Are you still seeing **specific console errors** after applying the changes

Description: negative — adding a geocoder to an existing Mapbox GL JS app
prompt: I use Mapbox GL JS v2 and want to add a geocoder search box to my map. What are my options?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
Below is a quick-reference guide that shows **all the practical ways you can add a search-box (geocoder) to a Mapbox GL JS v2 map**, together with the pros/cons of each approach, a minimal code example, and notes on licensing, rate-limits and migration to MapLibre later on. --- ## 1️⃣ The “official” way – **@mapbox/mapbox-gl-geocoder** | What it is | How it works | When to use it | Quick start | |------------|--------------|----------------|-------------| | An officially-maintained UI control that talks to the **Mapbox Geocoding API**. | The control creates an `` element, debounces the user’s typing, calls `https://api.mapbox.com/geocoding/v5/mapbox.places/.json?access_token=…` and returns a `MapboxGeocoderResult` object. | • You already have a Mapbox access token.
• You need the richest feature set (autocomplete, proximity bias, language, country filters, fuzzy matching, address-level results, etc.).
• You’re fine with Mapbox’s usage limits (50 k free requests / month, then paid). | ```bash\nnpm i @mapbox/mapbox-gl-geocoder\n```\n```js\nimport mapboxgl from 'mapbox-gl';\nimport MapboxGeocoder from '@mapbox/mapbox-gl-geocoder';\nimport '@mapbox/mapbox-gl-geocoder/dist/mapbox-gl-geocoder.css';\n\nmapboxgl.accessToken = 'YOUR_MAPBOX_TOKEN';\nconst map = new mapboxgl.Map({\n container: 'map',\n style: 'mapbox://styles/mapbox/streets-v12',\n center: [-122.42, 37.78],\n zoom: 12\n});\n\nconst geocoder = new MapboxGeocoder({\n accessToken: mapboxgl.accessToken,\n mapboxgl: mapboxgl, // required for the built-in UI\n placeholder: 'Search places…',\n proximity: { longitude: -122.42, latitude: 37.78 }, // optional bias\n countries: 'us', // optional filter\n language: 'en', // optional UI language\n});\n\nmap.addControl(geocoder, 'top-left');\n```\n*Result*: a ready-to-use search box that automatically flies the map to the chosen result (or you can listen to `result` events and handle it yourself).| ### Things to keep in mind | ✅ | ❌ | |---|---| | **Works out-of-the-box** with Mapbox GL JS v2 (no extra CSS changes). | **Tied to Mapbox services** – you must keep a valid token and respect Mapbox’s rate-limits. | | **Rich UI** – clear button, keyboard navigation, “use current location” button (if you enable `marker: true`). | **Proprietary** – not usable if you ever want to move to an open-source stack (MapLibre). | | **Customizable** – you can pass `bbox`, `filter`, `types`, `autocomplete: false`, etc. | **Large bundle** – the control adds ~30 KB gzipped (JS + CSS). | | **Internationalised** – `language` option works for many locales. | **No built-in reverse-geocode UI** – you have to call the API yourself if you need that. | --- ## 2️⃣ Call the **Mapbox Geocoding API** yourself (no UI library) If you only need a very lightweight UI (e.g., a plain `` styled by your own CSS) you can skip the plugin and hit the API directly. | Why you might do this | Example | |----------------------|---------| | You want a custom look-and-feel that the plugin can’t provide. | ```html\n\n```\n```js\nconst token = 'YOUR_MAPBOX_TOKEN';\nconst input = document.getElementById('search');\nlet abortCtrl = null;\ninput.addEventListener('input', debounce(async e => {\n const q = e.target.value.trim();\n if (!q) return;\n if (abortCtrl) abortCtrl.abort();\n abortCtrl = new AbortController();\n const url = `https://api.mapbox.com/geocoding/v5/mapbox.places/${encodeURIComponent(q)}.json?access_token=${token}&autocomplete=true&limit=5`;\n const resp = await fetch(url, { signal: abortCtrl.signal });\n const data = await resp.json();\n // render `data.features` however you like (list, dropdown, etc.)\n}, 300));\n\nfunction debounce(fn, wait) { let t; return (...a)=>{clearTimeout(t); t=setTimeout(()=>fn(...a),wait)}; }\n``` | | You need a **different response format** (e.g., you only want the `center` array). | Same code – just pick the fields you need from `data.features[i]`. | | You want to **combine multiple geocoders** (Mapbox + Nominatim) in one UI. | Call both APIs in parallel, merge the results, de-duplicate. | **Pros** * Minimal JS bundle (just a fetch + debounce). * Full control over UI/UX. **Cons** * You have to implement the dropdown, keyboard navigation, and “fly-to” logic yourself. * You still need a Mapbox token and are bound by Mapbox’s terms. --- ## 3️⃣ Open-source / free alternatives (no Mapbox token) If you want to **avoid Mapbox’s commercial API** (or you’re planning to migrate to MapLibre later), you can swap the backend while keeping the same UI component (or use a different UI library).
